title: Over-using Inline Directives (`#[inline(always)]`)
pattern: An author annotating every helper function or method with force-inline directives (`#[inline(always)]` or C++ `__forceinline`).
why_bad: It inflates the compiled binary size, causing instruction cache thrashing (L1i misses). It also prevents compiler-specific inter-procedural analysis, often resulting in slower machine code than normal compiler-directed inlining [339, 347, 348].
detection: Functions with a substantial number of operations or I/O calls marked with `#[inline(always)]`.
counterexample: Small wrapper functions (such as a single getter returning a field value) where inlining is guaranteed to remove call overhead. `Context-dependent`.
fix: Remove the manual inline directive and let the compiler's optimizer decide.
